relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It reports that Gja1 expression matches the phenotype of oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly, which is supporting evidence for this entry.

findings.statement: Richardson et al. (2004) reported that expression of Gja1 correlated with the phenotype seen in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.
quotes: Expression of Gja1 correlates with the phenotype observed in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.

relevance_reason: The title shows that the paper is about syndactyly of the ring and little fingers, the defining feature of syndactyly type III. Only the title was available, so no details about patients, families or inheritance could be extracted.

findings.statement: JOHNSTON and KIRBY (1955) reported syndactyly of the ring and little fingers.
quotes: Syndactyly of the ring and little finger.

phenotypes.text: syndactyly of the ring and little finger

relevance_reason: The abstract reports GJA1 mutations in oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODDD), a syndrome in which syndactyly type III occurs in some cases. This links SDTY3 to GJA1, but it does not report isolated syndactyly type III.

findings.statement: Paznekas et al. (2003) noted that oculodentodigital dysplasia is an autosomal dominant syndrome with craniofacial (ocular, nasal, and dental) and limb dysmorphisms, spastic paraplegia, and neurodegeneration. Syndactyly type III and conductive deafness can occur in some cases, and cardiac abnormalities are rarely seen.
quotes: This autosomal dominant syndrome presents with craniofacial (ocular, nasal, and dental) and limb dysmorphisms, spastic paraplegia, and neurodegeneration. Syndactyly type III and conductive deafness can occur in some cases, and cardiac abnormalities are observed in rare instances.

findings.statement: Paznekas et al. (2003) found GJA1 (connexin 43) mutations in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia that they screened. They found 16 different missense mutations and 1 codon duplication. The authors suggested that the mutations may cause misassembly of channels or alter channel conduction properties.
quotes: We found mutations in the GJA1 gene in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia that we screened. Sixteen different missense mutations and one codon duplication were detected.
These mutations may cause misassembly of channels or alter channel conduction properties.

relevance_reason: The paper mapped oculodentodigital syndrome to chromosome 6q22-q24. It also suggested that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same region, based on a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features.

findings.statement: Gladwin et al. (1997) studied a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features. Their analysis suggested that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same region of chromosome 6q22-q24 as the oculodentodigital syndrome (ODD) locus.
quotes: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features, further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.

findings.statement: Gladwin et al. (1997) noted that type III syndactyly occurs as part of oculodentodigital syndrome but has also been reported as an isolated entity. They found linkage of ODD to polymorphic markers on chromosome 6q (pairwise maximum lod score = 9.37 at theta = 0.001).
quotes: Type III syndactyly, which occurs as part of ODD, has also been reported to occur as an isolated entity.
linkage to polymorphic markers located on chromosome 6q established (pairwise Zmax = 9.37; theta = 0.001)

relevance_reason: The paper reports a large family with type III syndactyly (ring and little finger syndactyly) and shows that it is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

findings.statement: McKiernan and McCann (1993) reported a large family with 14 members who had familial syndactyly of the ring and little fingers (type III syndactyly). They found that the clinical features varied between affected members. Three affected members had surgery in the authors' unit, and the senior author had previously operated on a fourth elsewhere.
quotes: We present a pedigree containing 14 cases of familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger (Type III syndactyly).
Three of these were treated surgically in this unit, and a fourth had previously been treated elsewhere by the senior author of this paper.
clinical study reveals variable phenotypical expression

phenotypes.text: syndactyly of the ring and little fingers

findings.statement: McKiernan and McCann (1993) analyzed the pedigree of a large family with 14 members affected by type III syndactyly. They concluded that the analysis confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: Analysis of the pedigree confirms the autosomal dominant nature of the genetic defect

relevance_reason: Reports a three-generation family with type III syndactyly and mild oculodentodigital dysplasia features, suggesting that type III syndactyly falls within the ODDD clinical spectrum.

findings.statement: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) described a newborn boy with complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3 to 5 on the left hand and fingers 4 and 5 on the right hand. His mother and maternal grandmother had been born with the same hand malformation. The mother had a thin nose and small teeth. The grandmother's teeth had been very small, with enamel hypoplasia. Both women had normal eyes.
quotes: A newborn male patient presented with complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3-5 in the left hand and fingers 4-5 in the right hand. The mother and maternal grandmother were born with the same hand malformation.
Facial features in the mother showed a thin nose and small teeth; eyes were normal. In the grandmother, teeth had been very small with enamel hypoplasia; eyes were normal.

findings.statement: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) concluded that inheritance was autosomal dominant in a family in which syndactyly was passed down through 3 generations: maternal grandmother, mother and son.
quotes: The mother and maternal grandmother were born with the same hand malformation.
Inheritance is autosomal dominant.

findings.statement: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) concluded that the family showed variable expression of oculodentodigital dysplasia. They proposed that type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia form a clinical spectrum.
quotes: The present family provides evidence of the variable expression in oculodentodigital dysplasia.

relevance_reason: Reports new cases of isolated ring-little finger syndactyly (syndactyly type III), with inheritance and associated features.

findings.statement: De Smet et al. (1994) described 5 new cases of isolated syndactyly of the ring and small fingers. Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger was a frequent association, and the authors stated that surgery is required at a young age.
quotes: Five new cases of isolated syndactyly of the small and ring finger are described.
Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is a frequent association. Surgery is required at a young age.

phenotypes.text: isolated syndactyly of the ring and small fingers

phenotypes.hpo_label: Short middle phalanx of the 5th finger

findings.statement: De Smet et al. (1994) concluded that autosomal dominant inheritance was obvious in their cases of isolated ring-small finger syndactyly.
quotes: Autosomal dominant inheritance is obvious.

findings.statement: De Smet et al. (1994) stated that surgery is required at a young age for syndactyly of the ring and small fingers.
quotes: Surgery is required at a young age.

relevance_reason: Describes a Norwegian family with hereditary spastic paraplegia, neurogenic bladder and syndactyly. The abstract does not name the type of syndactyly, so it gives only context for syndactyly type III.

findings.statement: Opjordsmoen and Nyberg-Hansen (1980) reported a family from northern Norway in which 9 of 22 members across 3 generations had spastic paraplegia together with neurogenic bladder disturbance and syndactyly. The main complaint was the bladder disturbance, an incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis (uninhibited neurogenic bladder), which appeared early in the disease. The authors suggested that the family probably represented an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia.
quotes: a family settled in the northern part of Norway, with a hereditary neurological disorder consisting clinically of spastic paraplegia associated with neurogenic bladder disturbances and syndactylia. Nine out of 22 members in three generations exhibit these clinical features.
The bladder disturbances, being incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis (uninhibited neurogenic bladder), were the main complaint and occurred at an early stage of the disease.
The family probably represents an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP).

phenotypes.text: neurogenic bladder (uninhibited, incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis)

findings.statement: Opjordsmoen and Nyberg-Hansen (1980) concluded that the disorder of spastic paraplegia, neurogenic bladder and syndactyly in this 3-generation Norwegian family was inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
quotes: The mode of inheritance is considered to be autosomal dominant.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with type III syndactyly and ODDD-like facies, and discusses how the two conditions are related.

findings.statement: Brueton et al. (1990) described a family with type III syndactyly and a facial appearance resembling the facial phenotype of oculodentodigital dysplasia. The family had none of the other characteristic findings of oculodentodigital dysplasia.
quotes: A family is described with type III syndactyly and facies resembling the oculodentodigital dysplasia facial phenotype in the absence of any of the other characteristic findings of the latter condition.

findings.statement: Brueton et al. (1990) discussed how type III syndactyly relates to oculodentodigital dysplasia, asking whether they are separate genetic entities or part of one disease spectrum.
quotes: The relationship between type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia is discussed.
